subject: Strength of Materials
summary: the flexure formula, section modulus, T- and I-sections, beams of uniform strength, flitched beams and shear stress distributions

questions.text: Which of the following is not an assumption of the simple bending (flexure) theory σ/y = M/I = E/R?
opts: Plane sections remain plane after bending
The material is homogeneous and obeys Hooke's law
E is the same in tension and in compression
Bending stress varies parabolically across the depth
questions.ans: (D) Bending stress varies parabolically across the depth
solution: Concept: Plane sections remaining plane gives strain ε = y/R, which is linear in y.
With Hooke's law and the same E in tension and compression, σ = Ey/R is also linear in y, zero at the neutral axis.
A parabolic variation is the shape of the shear stress in a rectangular beam, not the bending stress.
Exam tip: Bending stress: linear, max at extreme fibres. Shear stress: parabolic (rectangle), max at the N.A.

questions.text: A rectangular beam 80 mm wide and 160 mm deep carries a bending moment of 8 kN·m about its horizontal axis. The maximum bending stress (in MPa, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: σmax = M/Z with Z = bd²/6.
σmax = 8 × 10⁶ / 3.413 × 10⁵ = 23.44 MPa (compression at top, tension at bottom for sagging).
Exam tip: Keep N and mm together: kN·m × 10⁶ = N·mm, and the answer is directly in MPa.

questions.text: The section modulus of a hollow circular section of outer diameter D and inner diameter d is
solution: Concept: Z = I/ymax, with ymax = D/2.
π(D³ − d³)/32 is the common wrong answer: section moduli cannot be subtracted like moments of inertia.
Exam tip: Subtract I's (same axis), never Z's.

questions.text: The T-section shown (flange 120 mm × 20 mm, web 20 mm × 100 mm) is used with the flange on top and carries a sagging bending moment of 6 kN·m. The maximum tensile bending stress (in MPa, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: Locate the centroid, find I about it (parallel-axis theorem), then σ = My/I at the extreme tension fibre.
Areas: flange 2400 mm² (centroid 10 mm from top), web 2000 mm² (centroid 70 mm from top).
ȳ from top = (2400 × 10 + 2000 × 70)/4400 = 37.27 mm; bottom fibre is 120 − 37.27 = 82.73 mm below the N.A.
Sagging → tension at the bottom: σt = 6 × 10⁶ × 82.73/5.674 × 10⁶ = 87.5 MPa; compression at the top is only 39.4 MPa.
Exam tip: For unsymmetric sections the two extreme stresses differ; always check which fibre governs.

questions.text: A solid circular beam of diameter 100 mm carries a shear force of 47.12 kN. The maximum shear stress in the section is nearly
solution: Concept: For a solid circle τmax = (4/3) τavg, at the neutral axis.
τmax = (4/3) × 6 = 8 MPa
Exam tip: Factors to remember: rectangle 3/2, circle 4/3, triangle 3/2 (at mid-height), diamond 9/8.

questions.text: The symmetric I-section shown (flanges 150 mm × 20 mm, web 10 mm thick, overall depth 300 mm) carries a shear force of 100 kN. The maximum shear stress in the section (in MPa, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: τ = VQ/(I t); the maximum is at the neutral axis, where the width t is the web thickness.
At the flange–web junction τ jumps from 2.1 MPa (in the flange, t = 150) to 31.7 MPa (in the web, t = 10). The web carries about 93 % of the shear.
Exam tip: A quick check: V/(web area) = 100000/(300 × 10) = 33.3 MPa is close to τmax for I-beams.

questions.text: If the width of a rectangular beam is doubled and its depth is halved (same material), its moment-carrying capacity becomes
solution: Concept: M = σZ and Z = bd²/6 ∝ bd².
New Z ∝ (2b)(d/2)² = bd²/2 → capacity becomes half.
Depth matters more than width because it enters squared.
Exam tip: Stiffness (I ∝ bd³) would fall to one-quarter in the same change.

questions.text: A steel wire of diameter 3 mm is to be bent into a circular arc. Taking E = 210 GPa, the smallest radius of curvature of the wire axis (in m) for which the bending stress does not exceed 210 MPa is ______
solution: Concept: From σ/y = E/R → R = E ymax/σ.
y<sub>max</sub> = 1.5 mm
Exam tip: If a drum radius is asked instead, subtract the wire radius: 1500 − 1.5 = 1498.5 mm.

questions.text: The strongest rectangular beam (in bending) that can be cut from a circular log of diameter D has a depth-to-width ratio of
solution: Concept: Maximise Z = bh²/6 with b² + h² = D².
Z ∝ b(D² − b²); dZ/db = D² − 3b² = 0 → b = D/√3, h = D√(2/3)
Exam tip: The stiffest beam (max I ∝ bh³) gives h/b = √3. Do not mix them up.

questions.text: A simply supported beam of span 4 m with a rectangular section 100 mm wide × 200 mm deep carries a single point load P at midspan. If the permissible bending stress is 12 MPa, the largest P (in kN) is ______
solution: Concept: Mmax = PL/4 at midspan; set Mmax = σZ.
Exam tip: Self-weight is ignored unless the question gives the density.

questions.text: In the flange of an I-beam carrying a vertical shear force, the horizontal shear stress (shear flow) along the flange width varies
opts: linearly from zero at the flange tip to a maximum at the web
parabolically, maximum at the flange tip
as a cubic, maximum at the flange tip
questions.ans: (A) linearly from zero at the flange tip to a maximum at the web
solution: Concept: In the flange, Q of the part from the tip to a cut at distance s is (s tf) × (h/2), which grows linearly with s.
τ = VQ/(I t<sub>f</sub>) ∝ s → zero at the free tip, maximum where the flange meets the web.
This flange shear flow is what locates the shear centre of channel sections.
Exam tip: In the web the variation is parabolic; in thin flanges it is linear.

questions.text: A beam has a square cross-section placed with one diagonal vertical (as shown) and carries a vertical shear force. The ratio of the maximum shear stress to the average shear stress is ______
solution: Concept: τ = VQ/(I b); for the diamond the width b falls towards the N.A. faster than Q grows near it, so τ peaks away from the N.A.
With half-diagonal h: b = 2(h − y), Q = (h − y)²(h + 2y)/3, so τ ∝ (h − y)(h + 2y); dτ/dy = 0 gives y = h/4 = d/8 from the N.A. (d = full diagonal)
τmax = (9/8) τavg = 1.125 τavg; at the N.A. itself τ = τavg.
Exam tip: Diamond and triangle are the two GATE favourites where τmax is not at the N.A.

questions.text: A simply supported beam carries a central point load. To be a beam of uniform strength with a constant depth, its width must vary along the span (from a support towards the centre)
opts: linearly with distance from the support
with the square root of the distance
with the square of the distance
questions.ans: (A) linearly with distance from the support
solution: Concept: Uniform strength: σ = 6M(x)/(b h²) is the same at every section.
M(x) = (P/2)x for 0 ≤ x ≤ L/2; with h fixed, b ∝ M ∝ x (linear).
With constant width instead, h² ∝ x → h ∝ √x.
Exam tip: Leaf springs are a practical form of such a constant-depth, varying-width beam.

questions.text: A flitched beam is made of a timber section 150 mm wide × 300 mm deep with a 10 mm × 300 mm steel plate bolted on each side (as shown). E<sub>steel</sub>/E<sub>timber</sub> = 20 and the permissible stresses are 8 MPa in timber and 150 MPa in steel. The moment of resistance of the beam (in kN·m, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Transform the steel into equivalent timber (width × m); strains are equal at the same depth, so σs = m σt at the same fibre.
Equivalent timber width = 150 + 20 × (2 × 10) = 550 mm; Z<sub>eq</sub> = 550 × 300²/6 = 8.25 × 10⁶ mm³
If timber reaches 8 MPa, steel would be 20 × 8 = 160 MPa > 150 MPa. So steel governs: σ<sub>t</sub> = 150/20 = 7.5 MPa at the extreme fibre.
Exam tip: Always check both materials; the one that reaches its limit first decides M.

questions.text: At the extreme top and bottom fibres of a beam section carrying both bending moment and shear force,
opts: bending stress is maximum and shear stress is zero
bending stress is zero and shear stress is maximum
questions.ans: (A) bending stress is maximum and shear stress is zero
solution: Concept: σ = My/I is largest at ymax.
The top and bottom surfaces are free of load, so by complementary shear the transverse shear stress there is zero.
At the N.A. the situation is reversed: σ = 0 and τ is (usually) maximum.
Exam tip: This is why principal-stress questions on beams take the extreme fibre as uniaxial.
